title: Quantum Tunneling: Wavepacket Penetration Through a Potential Energy Barrier
topic: Quantum Mechanics, Wave-Particle Duality & Schrödinger Equation
pedagogical_goal: Visually demonstrate the phenomenon of quantum tunneling, where a subatomic particle has a non-zero probability of passing directly through a potential energy barrier higher than the particle's kinetic energy (E < V0), impossible in classical mechanics. Illustrate the exponential attenuation of the evanescent wave inside the barrier and the relationship between barrier thickness, energy deficit, and transmission coefficient.

fundamental_laws: 1D Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation: -(\hbar^2 / 2m) * (d^2\psi / dx^2) + V(x)\psi = E\psi
Wavevector in Region I & III (E > 0): k = \sqrt{2mE} / \hbar
Decay Constant in Barrier Region II (V0 > E): \kappa = \sqrt{2m(V0 - E)} / \hbar
Transmission Coefficient (WKB approximation): T = exp(-2 * \kappa * L)
Exact Transmission Probability: T = 1 / (1 + (V0^2 * sinh^2(\kappa * L)) / (4 * E * (V0 - E)))

derived_formulas.transmission_probability: particle_energy >= barrier_height ? 1.0 : (1.0 / (1.0 + (Math.pow(barrier_height, 2) * Math.pow(Math.sinh(Math.min(15, 5.12 * Math.sqrt(Math.max(0.01, barrier_height - particle_energy)) * barrier_width * (particle_type === 'proton' ? 4.0 : (particle_type === 'muon' ? 2.0 : 1.0)))), 2)) / (4.0 * particle_energy * Math.max(0.05, barrier_height - particle_energy)))))
derived_formulas.tunneling_regime_label: particle_energy >= barrier_height ? 'Above-Barrier Transmission (Classical Pass)' : (transmission_probability < 0.01 ? 'Deep Evanescent Attenuation (R ≈ 100%)' : 'Measurable Quantum Tunneling (T > 1%)')

components.description: Cross-sectional potential energy profile V(x). Region I (x: 60-380) has V=0. Region II (x: 380 to 380+width*80) represents the glowing potential barrier of height V0 with semi-transparent violet-indigo gradient fill. Region III (after barrier) returns to V=0.
Cyan horizontal dashed line representing total particle energy E. Visually intersects the barrier height V0 to make the energy deficit (V0 - E) immediately apparent.

Continuous real-time Schrödinger wave function psi(x). Region I exhibits superposition of incident and reflected waves forming an interference standing wave pattern. Region II decays exponentially as exp(-kappa * x). Region III continues as a smooth sinusoidal oscillation with attenuated amplitude sqrt(T).

Shaded probability density curve |psi(x)|^2 showing the probability distribution of finding the particle at any spatial coordinate x, clearly demonstrating the finite non-zero probability to the right of the barrier.

Continuous stream of Gaussian quantum wavepackets/particles drifting from left to right. When hitting the barrier at x: 380, particles probabilistically bifurcate: the vast majority reflect backward with red trails, while a percentage matching T emerges on the right with green luminescence.
Comparison HUD displaying Newtonian Classical Mechanics (T = 0% strictly blocked by barrier) vs. Quantum Mechanics (T > 0% probabilistic wave penetration).

interactive_controls.label: Particle Energy (E)
interactive_controls.description: Adjust the total kinetic energy of the approaching quantum wavepacket.

interactive_controls.label: Barrier Potential (V₀)
interactive_controls.description: Adjust the electrostatic potential height of the barrier.

interactive_controls.label: Barrier Width (L)
interactive_controls.description: Adjust the physical barrier thickness. Notice the exponential sensitivity of tunneling probability to thickness.

interactive_controls.label: Particle Mass Category
interactive_controls.description: Select between Electron, Muon, and Proton to observe why heavy particles (protons) practically never tunnel in macroscopic systems.

interactive_controls.label: Display Mode
interactive_controls.description: Toggle between the wave function amplitude ψ(x), probability density |ψ(x)|², and particle packets.

telemetry_metrics.label: Tunneling Transmission (T)
telemetry_metrics.description: Percentage probability that a particle traverses the classically forbidden potential barrier.

telemetry_metrics.label: Reflection Probability (R)
telemetry_metrics.description: Percentage probability that the incident quantum wave is reflected back into Region I.

telemetry_metrics.label: Evanescent Decay Constant (κ)
telemetry_metrics.description: Exponential attenuation rate inside the barrier: ψ(x) ∝ exp(-κx).

telemetry_metrics.label: Penetration Depth (δ = 1/κ)
telemetry_metrics.description: Characteristic distance over which the wavefunction drops to 1/e (36.8%) of its initial value.

telemetry_metrics.label: Energy Barrier Deficit (V₀ - E)
telemetry_metrics.description: Height of the barrier above the particle energy. In classical physics, any positive value strictly blocks passage.

educational_cards.title: Why Does Quantum Tunneling Occur?
educational_cards.content: Unlike classical particles which bounce like billiard balls when particle energy E is less than V₀ (E < V₀), quantum particles possess wave-particle duality described by Schrödinger's wave equation. Because the wave function and its derivative must be continuous everywhere, the wave does not abruptly drop to zero at the barrier face; instead, it decays exponentially inside. If the barrier is thin enough, a non-zero tail emerges on the other side, giving the particle a real probability of appearing on the opposite side.

educational_cards.title: Exponential Thickness Sensitivity (The STM Principle)
educational_cards.content: Notice how increasing barrier thickness L from 0.8 nm to 1.6 nm causes tunneling probability T to collapse by orders of magnitude. This exponential sensitivity is the operating principle of the Scanning Tunneling Microscope (STM): changing the tip-to-surface distance by just 0.1 nm changes current by a factor of 10, enabling atomic-scale resolution.

educational_cards.title: Why Don't Everyday Objects Tunnel?
educational_cards.content: Switch the mass selector from Electron to Proton. Notice how transmission plunges to virtually zero. Because the decay constant κ scales with the square root of particle mass (\sqrt{m}), macroscopic objects like baseballs or humans (with masses > 10^27 times an electron) have tunneling probabilities so microscopic that one would have to wait longer than the age of the universe to observe an event.
